key_insight: You can accurately estimate the mean of a high-dimensional Gaussian even when each sample is only observed as the cell of a partition that contains it; the paper characterizes when this is possible and gives efficient algorithms with provable guarantees.
problem_solved: Estimating a Gaussian mean from "coarse" observations (each sample revealed only as a set/partition cell containing it) — a realistic challenge arising from rounding, limited sensor resolution, aggregation, and communication or privacy constraints.
method: Characterize identifiability and statistical limits: precise conditions and sample-complexity (minimax) bounds that determine when the mean can be recovered from partitioned observations.
Design efficient algorithms with provable error guarantees: polynomial-time procedures that achieve near-optimal estimation under the coarse-data model.
Validate theory empirically: simulations comparing estimation error versus sample size and partition coarseness, demonstrating robustness across dimensions and partition types.
impact: Provides practical tools and theory for learning from rounded, binned, or aggregated measurements, enabling robust parameter estimation in resource-constrained sensing, privacy-preserving data collection, and systems with coarse reporting.
visual_elements: Diagram of a 2D Gaussian with an overlaid partition: highlight a sample point and the cell reported (shows coarse observation vs true point).
Error-vs-sample-size plots comparing full-data estimation and coarse-data algorithms across different partition granularities.
Flowchart of the estimation pipeline: coarse input → algorithm (theoretical guarantee badge) → estimated mean, with callouts for sample complexity and runtime.
Icons depicting motivating applications: sensor with low resolution, rounded numeric display, and a privacy shield representing aggregated reporting.
paper_title: Mean Estimation from Coarse Data: Characterizations and Efficient Algorithms
paper_authors: Alkis Kalavasis, Anay Mehrotra, Manolis Zampetakis, Felix Zhou, Ziyu Zhu
